producer: Domaine du Closel – Château des Vaults
about: Château des Vaults stands in the village of Savennières, on the north bank of the Loire just downstream from Angers; its vineyard is first recorded in 1495. In the 20th century Bernard du Closel, mayor of the village for forty years, helped create the Savennières appellation in 1952, and the estate took his name. His niece Michèle de Jessey built the modern domaine, and from 2001 her daughter Evelyne de Pontbriand led it, served as president of the appellation and co-founded the Académie du Chenin.

Clos du Papillon is the estate’s flagship: a small, steep valley parcel, shared only with one neighbour, on sandy clay strewn with schist, volcanic rhyolite and quartz. The vines, 20 to 70 years old, give tiny yields and are farmed biodynamically (Demeter and Biodyvin certified since 2015). The grapes are picked by hand in two passes, pressed as whole clusters and fermented with native yeasts nearly to dryness; each lot then ages about a year on its lees in used 400-litre barrels before blending.

Savennières is Chenin Blanc at its most serious and dry, and Clos du Papillon is one of its reference sites. Tasting the 2022, Patricia Stefanowicz MW found golden apple, mirabelle and apricot with acacia honey and a creamy touch of oak, carried by racy acidity and long length. The wine won the top “Master” medal in the 2024 Chenin Blanc Masters.
